dependencies.statement:
Let $P$ be an admissible polygon whose boundary segments are all effective edges, and assume the edge moments in @lem-edge-moments. Then its first eigenfunction satisfies
$$
\int_P|\nabla u|^4=\lambda^2\left(\int_Pu^4-A(P)^{-1}\right).
$$
dependencies.title: Airy fourth-power identity

dependencies.statement:
There are universal constants $S_0,C>0$ such that, for normalized conformal data from @def-conformal-data with $S\le S_0$, if $v$ is the positive first solution of
$$
-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v\quad\text{in }\mathbb D,qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,qquad \int_{\mathbb D}v^2|1+g|^2=1,
$$
then, with $J$ as in @def-j-functional,
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+R(g),qquad |R(g)|\le CS^{3/2},
$$
where $\rho_n=jJ_{n+1}(j)/J_n(j)$ and $0<\rho_n<2$. In particular,
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}-1\ge S/6.
$$
dependencies.title: Uniform disk perturbation expansion

dependencies.statement:
Let $P$ be admissible and stationary in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon. If $u>0$ is the $L^2$-normalized first eigenfunction, $\lambda=\lambda_1(P)$, $c=\lambda/A(P)$, and $q=|\partial_\nu u|^2$, then every effective edge $E$, parametrized by physical arclength $s\in[0,\ell_E]$, satisfies
$$
\int_E(q-c)\,ds=0,\qquad \int_Es(q-c)\,ds=0.
$$
dependencies.title: Stationary edge moments

target.proof:
Under the edge-moment hypotheses @lem-edge-moments, pull @lem-airy-identity back by $F$ and use $F'^{-1}=1+k$ to obtain
$$
\int_{\mathbb D}|\nabla v|^4|1+k|^2
=\lambda^2\int_{\mathbb D}v^4|1+g|^2-\frac{\lambda^2}{\pi(1+S)}.
$$
The expansion supplied by @lem-disk-perturbation gives, in the weighted integrals below,
$$
|\nabla v|^4=a+b_1+R_1,
\qquad a=|\nabla v_0|^4,
\qquad \int_0^{2\pi}b_1(r,\theta)\,d\theta=0,
\qquad \|R_1\|_{L^1(\mathbb D)}\le CS.
$$
The function $a$ is radial and bounded below on a fixed outer annulus. Since the constant Fourier coefficient of $k$ vanishes, angular orthogonality removes the linear term $\int a\operatorname{Re}k$; the remaining principal term is $\int a|k|^2$. On a fixed inner disk, the Bergman pointwise estimate and $k=-g/(1+g)$ give $|k|\le C\sqrt S$, while on the outer annulus the lower bound for $a$ controls $\|k\|_{L^2}^2=T$ up to the displayed error. Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the $b_1$ and $R_1$ terms and the perturbation bounds therefore give
$$
T\le C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.
$$
Young's inequality absorbs the mixed term and, for sufficiently small $S$, the last two terms, proving $T\le CS$.
target.statement:
For the conformal data in @def-conformal-data of a stationary polygon whose canonical boundary presentation consists entirely of effective edges, satisfying @lem-edge-moments and @lem-disk-perturbation, and in the regime of @lem-near-circle-conformal, one has
$$
T\le CS.
$$
The constant is independent of the number and separation of the vertices and of the angle sizes.
target.title: Inverse derivative energy

critical_errors: @lem-disk-perturbation does not imply |∇v|⁴=a+b₁+R₁, the zero angular mean of b₁, or an L¹ bound on R₁. Treating that lemma as supplying these statements is an invalid dependency use.

The cancellation of ∫a Re(k), the inner-disk estimate |k|≤C√S, and the control of T by the outer-annulus integral are neither stated in the dependencies nor derived. The relation k=−g/(1+g) alone does not imply that k has zero constant Fourier coefficient.

The displayed scalar J(P) expansion supplies no bounds for the weighted b₁ and R₁ terms or for the right-hand side of the pulled-back identity. Consequently the asserted inequality T≤C{S+√S√T+√S T+ST} does not follow from the supplied material.
gaps: The packet supplies no semantic definitions for the conformal data, F, g, k, S, T, v, v₀, or J, so the normalization and claimed identities cannot be independently checked.
The conformal change of variables and the replacement A(P)^{-1}=1/[π(1+S)] are asserted without stating the needed normalization and relations.
Uniformity of the annulus bounds and constants with respect to vertices, separations, and angles is asserted rather than established.
report.repair_hints: Supply dependencies or proofs establishing the gradient perturbation expansion, Fourier normalization of k, Bergman and denominator bounds, and the weighted estimates leading to the displayed inequality. Also include the semantic conformal-data definitions and explicitly verify the pullback and area normalization.
report.summary: The proof relies on load-bearing claims that are not contained in the supplied dependencies. In particular, the disk-perturbation lemma gives only a scalar expansion for J(P), not the gradient decomposition and estimates used to control T.
